title: First part under budget
prompt:
A customer wants the first part on the shelf that costs less than their budget. Write `first_under(prices, budget)`. It checks the prices from left to right and gives back a pair: the position of the first price below the budget (or `-1` if there is none) and how many prices it looked at.

That is a linear search with a counter. When it works, `python3 cheap.py` prints `(3, 4)` and then `(-1, 5)`.
hints: You need two things as you walk the shelf: the position you are at, and a count of looks. `for i in range(len(prices)):` gives you the position.
Add 1 to `looks` every time you check a price. If `prices[i] < budget`, you are done: `return i, looks`.
Start with `looks = 0`. Inside the loop: `looks = looks + 1`, then the `if`. After the loop ends without finding one, `return -1, looks`.
explain_after: You wrote a linear search: start at the left and check each item in turn, the way the CS50 notes walk past doors from left to right [py-131]. When nothing matches, it has to look at every price, so the number of looks grows with the length of the shelf. Big O calls that O(n) [py-133].
